Title: On the Stability of Checkpoint Averaging Under Learning-Rate Warm Restarts

Authors: Chidi Okonkwo
Abstract: Averaging the weights of several checkpoints is a cheap way to improve generalization, but it is known to fail when the checkpoints lie in different basins of the loss surface. We analyse checkpoint averaging when training uses cosine schedules with warm restarts, and we show that the averaged model is stable, in the sense that its loss is within a constant factor of the best checkpoint, whenever the restart period exceeds a threshold that depends only on the sharpness at the end of each cycle. The bound is tight for quadratic objectives, and in experiments on image classification and small language models it predicts the restart period at which averaging stops helping to within twenty percent. These results suggest a simple rule for choosing which checkpoints to average, which we compare against greedy soups and exponential moving averages.
Comments:9 pages, 4 figures, appendix with proofs
